messages:
Maya: Quick thought — can we try a bisection-style canary for the next rollout? start 5% -> 25% -> 60% with automated checks and an explicit quarantine state if things look odd. planning doc soon.
Alex: +1. main concern is cache warmup mismatch between variants — cold prefixes will penalize the new variant.
Sophia: Agreed on warmup mismatch. Can we minimize duplicate compute by sampling shadow requests instead of full warmup?
Liam: Shadowing helps but costs. Another idea: targeted KV prefix seeding for heavy tenants so they see warmed caches early.
Maya: Targeted seeding seems good. fallback cost tradeoff though. For small tenants, sample-based shadowing + smaller warmup window.
Alex: Operationally we need abort rules: auto-abort if error_rate > X OR p95 latency delta > Y over window Z. Who defines defaults?
Sophia: Propose default aborts in runtime config: error_rate > 3% OR p95 increase > 20% over 5m. Teams can override per-deploy.
infra-bot: deploy 3445678901 initiated by Maya — canary rollout 5% started. monitoring: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollouts/3445678901
Liam: Also think about quality vs perf decisions: sometimes latency reg is acceptable for big quality wins. need manual hold.
Maya: I propose a QUARANTINE state: stop serving traffic, keep candidate live, collect metrics, run manual evals and probes. Allows human judgement before rollback.
Alex: API surface sketch: rollout.create({percent_steps:[5,25,60], mode:'bisection', abort_rules:[...], buy_in:'auto'|'manual'}) and rollout.update/abort endpoints.
Sophia: Add probe hooks: pull an eval harness after each step to compare quality metrics (bleu/ROUGE/LL? or task-specific), and factor into decision.
Liam: Example abort rule syntax: metric:error_rate window:5m op:> value:0.03. Let's codify schema and validate at create-time.
Maya: I'll PR an RFC with a state machine: INIT -> WARMUP (shadowing/prefix-seed) -> PERCENTED -> QUARANTINE -> ROLLFORWARD / ROLLBACK. Include probe integration + operator overrides.
Alex: Also add network/regional partition case: if cross-region latency skyrockets, runtime should fallback to nearest-stable-region variant automatically.
Sophia: Good catch. Need TTL for stale KVs if we switch regions.
Liam: For observability: require per-step snapshot (latency/error/quality) and a diff UI. Also enable fast manual flip that keeps canary metadata for audit.
Maya: I'll include runbook snippets for oncall: how to triage a quarantine, how to run manual evals, and how to perform a safe rollback.
Alex: One more: graceful degradation knob — if rates drop, prefer failover to cheaper small-quantized variant rather than full rollback.
Sophia: Put that behind a policy flag. Default is full rollback unless cost-aware failover enabled.
Maya: Filing issue now to capture config defaults + RFC link. Thanks y'all :rocket:
Liam: thanks — looking forward to the RFC.
